description.main: Catalogue of the exhibition at Gagosian, Paris (2016-17), of Cy Twombly's paintings and works on paper on the figure of Orpheus, 1968-1979. Texts by Giorgio Agamben and Gary D. Astrachan, with poems from Rilke's Sonnets to Orpheus.
description.extended:
The catalogue of a 2016-17 exhibition at Gagosian, Paris, that gathered Cy Twombly's paintings and works on paper on the figure of Orpheus, made between 1968 and 1979.

Edited by Mark Francis and designed by John Morgan studio, London, the cloth-bound volume has an essay by Giorgio Agamben in English and Italian, printed on four inserted pages, and an essay by Gary D. Astrachan in English. Poems from Rainer Maria Rilke's Sonnets to Orpheus appear in German and English. The exhibition ran from December 1, 2016 to April 22, 2017. Pureprint Group in Uckfield, England, printed the book.

Gagosian describes Orpheus in these works as a figure for both the artist and the creative process. Two sources shaped Twombly's treatment of the myth. One was Rilke's cycle of fifty-five poems, written in 1922. The other was The Veil of Orpheus (1953), a musique concrète composition by the French composer Pierre Henry. Astrachan later wrote a book on the artist, Naming the Gods: Cy Twombly's Passionate Poiesis (2020).
description.artist_bio: Cy Twombly (1928-2011), American artist, represented by Gagosian.
